draft.title: Classifying triangles
card: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides. An isosceles triangle has at least 2 equal sides. A scalene triangle has no equal sides.
An acute triangle has 3 angles less than 90°. A right triangle has one angle of exactly 90°. An obtuse triangle has one angle greater than 90°.
The angles in any triangle add to 180°. So a triangle can have at most one right angle or one obtuse angle.
A triangle has angles 50°, 50° and 80°. All are less than 90°, so it is acute. Two angles are equal, so two sides are equal, so it is isosceles.
draft.remember: Name a triangle by its sides and by its angles. Each name answers a different question.

a.q: A triangle has side lengths 5 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. How is it classified by its sides?
a.why: All three sides are different lengths, so the triangle is scalene. It is not isosceles, because that needs at least 2 equal sides. Right describes an angle, not a side.
a.clue: Compare the three side lengths. Are any equal?

b.q: A triangle has angles of 40°, 40° and 100°. How is it classified by its angles and by its sides?
b.why: The 100° angle is greater than 90°, so the triangle is obtuse. Two angles are equal, so two sides are equal, which makes it isosceles. It is not acute, because one angle is over 90°.
b.clue: Look for an angle over 90°, then for equal angles.
